newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ's Archer says monetary conditions too loose.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ's Archer says monetary conditions too loose.

text.p: Reserve Bank of New Zealand's Chief Financial Manager David Archer said on Monday that Monetary Conditions were too loose.

"Overall monetary conditions have become too loose, given our current monetary policy stance," Archer said in a statement. "Consistent with the approach the bank set out in June, we have been allowing monetary conditions increasing room to move as the quarter has progressed, and as our last complete look at inflation pressures becomes more distant.
"We have also been waiting to see whether the drift in conditions in recent days would reverse.
"It hasn't, leaving overall conditions beyond levels that we are comfortable with.
"As usual, the bank remains ready to act if necessary," Archer concluded.
Just prior to the bank's 1.00 p.m. (0100 GMT) statement, the bank's monetary conditions index was 125 basis points below the bank's stated desired level of 825 for the September quarter.
Shortly after Archer's comments the index rose to -102 at 723.
